1
A paperback book contains 210 sheets of paper (pages). Its thickness is measured with a ruler,
as shown.
book
1
0 cm
2
3
4
5
6
What is the average thickness of one sheet of the paper in the book?
A
0.013 mm
B
0.017 mm
C
0.13 mm
D
0.17 mm

hints: Look at the cm ruler under the book and read the positions of the left edge near $1\text{ cm}$ and the right edge near $3.5\text{ cm}$ to get the total thickness.
Recall that total thickness divided by $210$ sheets gives one sheet, and that $1\text{ cm} = 10\text{ mm}$ so the final answer must be in $\text{mm}$.
Calculate the difference in $\text{cm}$, multiply by $10$ to get about $27\text{ mm}$, then divide by $210$ and check whether your result is near $0.1\text{ mm}$ or $0.01\text{ mm}$.
walkthrough: Read the ruler for the book thickness. The left face is at about $0.9\text{ cm}$ and the right face is at about $3.6\text{ cm}$.
Find the total thickness by subtraction: $3.6\text{ cm} - 0.9\text{ cm} = 2.7\text{ cm}$.
Convert to $\text{mm}$ because one sheet is very thin: $2.7\text{ cm} \times 10 = 27\text{ mm}$.
Divide the total by the number of sheets to average: $27\text{ mm} / 210 \approx 0.1286\text{ mm}$.
Round to two significant figures, about $0.13\text{ mm}$, which checks as sensible for paper. This is option C.

A.explanation: Too small by a factor of 10, from an error converting $\text{cm}$ to $\text{mm}$ when finding the thickness of one sheet.

B.explanation: Too small by a factor of 10, from dividing the $27\text{ mm}$ total by the wrong number or misplacing the decimal in the $\text{cm}$ to $\text{mm}$ conversion.

C.explanation: Matches $27\text{ mm}$ divided by $210$ sheets, giving about $0.13\text{ mm}$ per sheet.

D.explanation: Too large because it uses about $3.6\text{ cm}$ as the thickness instead of subtracting the $0.9\text{ cm}$ starting position on the ruler.
